rubric_cards.title: Plan-PRD Alignment
rubric_cards.claim: Plan scope covers planning-review and implementation-review gates per PRD S6 mandate, with sidecar paths matching §6.3 artifact contract and 3-iteration cap matching §6.5.
rubric_cards.evidence: P1-T1 adds planning-review and implementation-review nodes. Plan references docs/plans/_advisory-reviews/ and _peer-reviews/ matching PRD §6.3. Plan peer_review metadata block (workflow YAML lines 530-536) already includes max_iterations: 3. Architecture diagram shows refine-plan → planning-review → implement-setup → code-review → implementation-review → live-validate → compose-finalize.
rubric_cards.disposition: present — scope and artifact paths align with PRD and design doc requirements

rubric_cards.title: Verify Command Sufficiency
rubric_cards.claim: All verify commands are executable and non-prose: workflow validation CLI, ripgrep node ID checks, bun test for bundled-defaults and loader tests.
rubric_cards.evidence: P1-T1: 'bun run cli validate workflows archon-piv-loop-codex-v2 --json' and 'rg -n id: planning-review|... .archon/workflows/defaults/archon-piv-loop-codex-v2.yaml'. P1-T2: 'bun test packages/workflows/src/defaults/bundled-defaults.test.ts' and 'bun test packages/workflows/src/loader.test.ts'. Both test files confirmed to exist with relevant coverage (loader.test.ts line 1630-1664 covers loop parsing, bundled-defaults.test.ts lines 36-71 cover bundle drift).
rubric_cards.disposition: present — all commands are grounded and executable

rubric_cards.title: Implementation-Review Positioning Clarity
rubric_cards.claim: The plan's architecture diagram and task description leave ambiguous whether implementation-review sits before or after fix-feedback iterations.
rubric_cards.evidence: Architecture diagram chain: code-review → implementation-review → live-validate. But fix-feedback node (workflow YAML lines 1220-1363, max_iterations: 10) sits between code-review and live-validate in the current YAML. The plan does not specify whether implementation-review precedes or follows fix-feedback. PRD §6.5 says 'implementation review is required after code validation and before final closeout' — design doc §8.2 clarifies 'after code is written and code validation has run, but before final closeout', which is consistent with post-fix-feedback placement but the plan doesn't make this explicit.
rubric_cards.disposition: partial — position is inferrable from PRD/design but not stated in the plan artifact itself

issues.title: Implementation-review position relative to fix-feedback is ambiguous
issues.details: The architecture diagram shows code-review → implementation-review → live-validate but omits fix-feedback from the chain entirely. The current workflow YAML has fix-feedback (max_iterations: 10) between code-review and live-validate. P1-T1 does not specify whether the new implementation-review node should precede or follow fix-feedback iterations. PRD §6.5 says 'after code validation and before final closeout'; design doc §8.2 says 'after code is written and code validation has run, but before final closeout' — both are consistent with post-fix-feedback placement but the plan should make this explicit.
issues.suggested_fix: Add one sentence to P1-T1 specifying implementation-review depends_on fix-feedback (or code-review if pre-loop), and update the architecture diagram to include fix-feedback in the node chain.

issues.title: Grounding snapshot flags fix-feedback max_iterations: 10 without disposition
issues.details: The plan's grounding section correctly identifies that fix-feedback has max_iterations: 10 on the integration base, but does not state whether S6 should change this value (PRD §6.5 caps material review/fix loops at 3 iterations) or leave it for a separate scope.
issues.suggested_fix: Add a one-line disposition in the grounding or non-goals section: either 'fix-feedback iteration cap is out of S6 scope' or 'P1-T1 will also set fix-feedback max_iterations to 3 per PRD §6.5'.

issues.details: state.json has authoring_state: 'drafted' while the markdown frontmatter has status: 'draft'. These likely represent the same state but use different terms. This is cosmetic and not a freeze blocker.
issues.suggested_fix: No action required unless the workflow tooling enforces exact term parity.
